rubrics.justification: Generally cautious and mostly compatible with a blastocyst assessment, but it soft-pedals visible features: the image appears somewhat collapsed/partially contracted and not clearly hatching despite the provided 4AA label. ICM/TE comments are reasonable but not especially precise to the image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, prior cycle history, semen parameters, endometrium, diagnosis, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with appropriate emphasis on morphology versus aneuploidy uncertainty. Minor issue: implantation/live birth figures are somewhat conservative relative to a reported 4AA embryo in a favorable 35-year-old.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with ASRM/ESHRE-style practice: respect lab grading, favor single embryo transfer, avoid bed rest, and avoid overtesting after one failure. Slight limitation is somewhat generic discussion of luteal support and PGT-A indications.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning after failure, including SET, routine luteal support, and review of transfer conditions. Useful, though not highly tailored beyond standard IVF management.
